\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Cryptography.SecretSharing.Vector}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Coordinatewise Shamir scheme]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.vecScheme}
\statementsource{AL17}{pdf-27f2b3787521-p004-b002}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.vecScheme}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme, TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.scheme}
Let $F$ be a field, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $\iota$ be an index type. The
vector-valued scheme shares a secret $v\colon\iota\to F$ using randomness that assigns
to each coordinate a polynomial of degree less than $k-1$, applying the Shamir scheme
separately in each coordinate. Given a finite set of parties and their share vectors, it
reconstructs the secret coordinate by coordinate using the Shamir reconstruction map.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinatewise vector sharing]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.isSharing_vecScheme}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.isSharing_vecScheme}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing, TCSlib.Shamir.isSharing_share, TCSlib.Shamir.vecScheme}
\difficulty{1}
Let $F$ be a field, let $k>0$, let $\iota$ be an index type, and let $v$ assign a field
element to each index and $q$ assign a polynomial of degree less than $k-1$ to each
index. For any fixed $x\in\iota$, the shares at coordinate $x$ produced by the vector
Shamir scheme form a sharing of $v(x)$ with degree bound less than $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness for vector secrets]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.vecScheme_correct}
\statementsource{AL17}{pdf-27f2b3787521-p004-b002}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.vecScheme_correct}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure.threshold, TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme.Correct, TCSlib.Shamir.correct, TCSlib.Shamir.vecScheme}
\difficulty{3}
Let $F$ be a field, let $k>0$, and let $\iota$ be any type. In the vector-valued sharing
scheme, for every finite set $A$ of nonzero field elements with at least $k$ members,
every secret $v:\iota\to F$, and every randomness function assigning a polynomial of
degree less than $k-1$ to each coordinate, reconstruction from the shares of $A$ returns
$v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Perfect privacy for vector secrets]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.vecScheme_perfectPrivacy}
\statementsource{AL17}{
  pdf-27f2b3787521-p013-b003,
  pdf-27f2b3787521-p014-b002
}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.vecScheme_perfectPrivacy}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure.threshold, TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme.PerfectPrivacy, TCSlib.Shamir.perfectPrivacy, TCSlib.Shamir.vecScheme}
\difficulty{4}
Let $F$ be a field, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $\iota$ be any type. For every
finite set $B$ of nonzero field elements with fewer than $k$ members and every pair of
secrets $v,v':\iota\to F$, there is a bijection from the randomness space to itself such
that, for every randomness choice and every party in $B$, the share of $v'$ under the
transformed randomness equals the share of $v$ under the original randomness.
\end{theorem}
